title: Console Circuit — Weekly Briefing (UI / Rollouts / Analytics)
summary: Weekly sync focused on stabilizing the new rollout gating (canary + A/B), trimming UI render hotspots, and the analytics pipeline backfill plan after the weekend spike.
body:
Date: 2026-12-28
Facilitator: Lena Park
Attendees: Lena (owner), Jonah, Priya, Evan, Sofia, Arjun (notes)
Length: 35m

Agenda:
- Quick status: UI, Rollouts, Analytics (3m each)
- Incident follow-up: canary telemetry spike on 2026-12-26
- Decisions for next rollout: gating thresholds and fallback policy
- Analytics backfill plan and cost estimate
- Action items and owners

Quick updates (one-liners):
- UI: Jonah — trimmed two render waterfall hotspots in panel list; measured 18% p95 widget CPU drop in local repro. PR 2890 ready for small QA smoke.
- Rollouts: Priya — new gating rule prototype (latency+error composite) passed canary in eu-west for 12h; observed higher feature flag churn in canaries. Need tweak.
- Analytics: Evan — ingestion lag observed during weekend spike (approx 14m tail), pipeline memory throttling suspected; backfill strategy drafted.

Incident recap (2026-12-26 telemetry spike):
- What happened: A traffic surge from a partner integration caused a high-cardinality metric burst (panel-open events) which cascaded into increased latency on the telemetry ingestion path and raised canary false-positive rate.
- Impact: Canary gating tripped for one rollout, UI latency blip for ~22 minutes in us-west, alerts routed to SRE.
- Root cause hypothesis: sampling disabled in partner integration + analytics worker memory pressure during high cardinality ingestion.
- Temporary mitigation applied: emergency sampling and soft-fail on gating (allowlist for affected partner).
- Long-term: add adaptive sampling, tighten backpressure from ingestion to metrics storage, and add a canary noise filter.

Decisions made in meeting:
- Keep new composite gating (latency+error) but add a noise filter that ignores spikes from known-senders for first 30m of canary. (Owner: Priya)
- Ship UI PR 2890 behind feature flag; roll out to 10% of org users for 24h before wider rollout. (Owner: Jonah)
- Start analytics backfill in low-cost window (2am-6am PST) with a single-tenant throttle to avoid repeated memory pressure. Backfill to be run incremental, 2h slices. (Owner: Evan)

Risk notes:
- If partner integrations continue to send high-cardinality payloads, sampling & noise filters may be insufficient — consider hard rate-limits and partner SLA enforcement (eng + biz).
- Feature-flag churn during canary makes gating noisy; need a lightweight audit trail for flag toggles tied to rollouts.

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya — implement noise filter in gating prototype and add unit tests (due 2027-01-03)
- Jonah — merge PR 2890 behind ff, coordinate QA and enable 10% rollout (due 2026-12-31)
- Evan — finalize backfill runbook, include cost estimate and retry policy, and schedule first backfill window (due 2027-01-02)
- Sofia — update incident postmortem stub in Confluence with timeline and initial hypotheses (due 2026-12-30)
- Arjun — open partner outreach doc and proposed rate-limit language for PM review (due 2027-01-05)

Notes to self / loose thoughts:
- Consider adding event cardinality telemetry to the Console SDK so we can proactively detect high-cardinality publisher behavior before it hits the ingestion path.
- For the gating composite score, experiment with a decaying score so a single large spike doesn't permanently bias canary decisions.
- Could use lightweight bloom-filter based sender caching to quickly identify noisy senders at ingress.

Follow-ups / next meeting:
- Quick sync Mon 2026-12-29 (15m) to confirm PR 2890 rollout progress and whether backfill window is green.
- Full reconvene Tuesday weekly channel for post-backfill review and to finalize canary noise filter metrics.

Referenced tickets & PRs:
- RB-4521 (canary gating prototype)
- RB-4678 (analytics pipeline memory throttling investigation)
- GH PR 2890 (panel render optimizations)

Tone: working draft — still noisy, contains action items and open questions.

End of briefing.
